images.caption: View of the West Coast region of the Western Cape, South Africa, taken during ISS Expedition 6. The vicinity of Cape Columbine is depicted, with associated beaches, bays and other water features. The inland area is mainly flat, but low hills including Karringberg (176 m) and Massenberg (160 m) fringe Saldanha Bay. Flanking the bay entrance are also the prominent landmarks of Malgaskop (112 m) and Postberg (193 m).
images.alt: View of the West Coast region of the Western Cape, South Africa, taken during ISS Expedition 6. The vicinity of Cape Columbine is depicted, with associated beaches, bays and other water features. The inland area is mainly flat, but low hills including Karringberg (176 m) and Massenberg (160 m) fringe Saldanha Bay. Flanking the bay entrance are also the prominent landmarks of Malgaskop (112 m) and Postberg (193 m).
images.artist: Earth Science and Remote Sensing Unit, Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center

images.filename: ISS006-E-37018 - View of South Africa, Saldanha Bay & Langebaan Lagoon.jpg
images.caption: A view of the West Coast region of the Western Cape, South Africa, taken during ISS Expedition 6. It shows Danger Bay, Saldanha Bay and Langebaan Lagoon.   Aquarius MOGS Saldanha, situated on the eastern shore of the bay, operates a major crude oil storage and in-tank blending terminal. It provides vital logistics for the global oil market by linking the Atlantic and Indian Ocean shipping routes. In 2025 it is owned by Aquarius Energy.
images.alt: A view of the West Coast region of the Western Cape, South Africa, taken during ISS Expedition 6. It shows Danger Bay, Saldanha Bay and Langebaan Lagoon.   Aquarius MOGS Saldanha, situated on the eastern shore of the bay, operates a major crude oil storage and in-tank blending terminal. It provides vital logistics for the global oil market by linking the Atlantic and Indian Ocean shipping routes. In 2025 it is owned by Aquarius Energy.
